outline.chapter_title: 1. Foundations of Language Modeling and Alignment
outline.description: An overview of transformer‑based language models, their capabilities, and the need for controllable behavior. This chapter introduces the concepts of unsupervised pre‑training, instruction tuning, and the alignment problem that motivates the rest of the book.
subtopics: Large‑scale unsupervised LM pre‑training
Instruction fine‑tuning and zero‑shot capabilities
The alignment challenge: safety, performance, controllability
Human preferences as a proxy for desired behavior
Limitations of naïve supervised fine‑tuning

outline.chapter_title: 2. From Human Feedback to Reinforcement Learning
outline.description: A historical perspective on learning from human preferences, the RLHF pipeline, and the role of reward modeling. The chapter describes how preference data is collected and turned into a reward function that can be optimised with RL.
subtopics: Human preference data collection (paired completions)
Bradley‑Terry and Plackett‑Luce models for preferences
Maximum‑likelihood reward learning (binary cross‑entropy)
KL‑constrained RL objective for policy optimisation
Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) in RLHF

outline.description: An in‑depth look at the mathematics behind the constrained RL problem that underlies RLHF and how it can be expressed in terms of reward functions and optimal policies.
subtopics: Formulation of the constrained RL objective
Derivation of the optimal policy under a KL penalty
Partition function and its role in policy definition
Exact solution for log‑linear reward models
Implications for discrete language generation

outline.description: Presentation of the key insight that a particular re‑parameterisation of the reward function enables direct optimisation of the policy without an explicit reward model or RL loop.
subtopics: Change‑of‑variables from reward to policy
Re‑parameterised reward: r = β log (π/π_ref) + β log Z(x)
Cancellation of the partition function in BT likelihood
Derivation of the DPO loss function
Relationship to OLS policy and KL‑regularised objective

outline.description: Step‑by‑step description of how to implement DPO, from data preparation to training, hyperparameters, and computational considerations.
subtopics: Preparation of preference dataset (paired responses)
Choice of reference policy π_ref (SFT or pseudo‑SFT)
Training objective: binary cross‑entropy with dynamic importance weight
β hyper‑parameter and its effect on KL constraint
Efficient probability estimation for generated sequences
Handling long‑form generation and batching

outline.chapter_title: 6. Comparing DPO to RLHF with PPO
outline.description: A comparative analysis of the two frameworks, highlighting theoretical differences, practical advantages, and trade‑offs in performance and stability.
subtopics: Single‑stage vs. multi‑stage pipelines
Gradient‑variance and baselines in actor‑critic vs. DPO
Normalisation term as soft‑value function
Empirical reward‑KL trade‑off curves
Common failure modes of PPO (mode collapse, hyper‑parameter sensitivity)

outline.description: Summary of the key experiments presented in the paper, detailing datasets, tasks, evaluation metrics, and results.
subtopics: Controlled sentiment generation (IMDb) and true reward function
Summarization (Reddit TL;DR) and human preference data
Single‑turn dialogue (Anthropic HH) and GPT‑4 evaluation
Hyper‑parameter sweeps and convergence plots
Comparison with SFT, Preferred‑FT, unlikelihood, PPO, Best‑of‑N baselines

outline.description: Explains how human judgment and GPT‑4 judgments were used to validate the quality of the refined models and discusses the design of prompts and inter‑rater agreement.
subtopics: Human evaluation protocol and interface
GPT‑4 as proxy evaluator (S vs. C prompts)
Correlation analysis with human agreement
Win‑rate definition and its interpretation

outline.chapter_title: 9. Theoretical Guarantees and Properties of DPO
outline.description: A deeper dive into the theoretical results proved in the paper, including equivalence classes of rewards, consistency proofs, and discussion of under‑specification.
subtopics: Equivalence relation on reward functions
Lemma: same preferences for equivalent rewards
Lemma: same optimal policy for equivalent rewards
Theorem: all reward classes represented by DPO re‑parameterisation
Discussion of identifiability and normalisation

outline.chapter_title: 10. Limitations, Future Work, and Practical Advice
outline.description: Critical assessment of DPO’s scope, open research questions, and guidance for practitioners who want to apply the method to new domains or larger models.
subtopics: Out‑of‑distribution generalisation
Scaling to larger models and multimodal data
Self‑labeling and curriculum learning opportunities
Potential over‑optimisation and mode collapse
Choosing β and reference policy in practice
Computational cost comparison with RLHF

outline.description: Wrap‑up of the main take‑aways, emphasising how DPO simplifies policy learning from preferences and its implications for building safer, more controllable language models.
subtopics: Summarisation of DPO contributions
Practical simplicity and computational efficiency
Impact on the alignment research community
Future directions beyond language modelling
